pointers.sentence: `Settings.__init__` warns for each that the settings module defines, attributed to the first frame outside Django (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).

`LazySettings.configure`, `override_settings` and an assignment to `settings` set values through `UserSettingsHolder.__setattr__` or `LazySettings.__setattr__`, which warn only when the code that set the value is outside Django (`django/conf/__init__.py:_show_settings_deprecation_warning`).

Where the project defines `MAILERS`, the read raises `AttributeError` instead, and `LazySettings.__dir__` leaves their defaults out of `dir(settings)` (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`, `django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__dir__`).

Where the project defines `MAILERS`, the read raises `AttributeError` instead, and `LazySettings.__dir__` leaves their defaults out of `dir(settings)` (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`, `django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__dir__`).

Defining both is refused with `ImproperlyConfigured` in the settings module or in one call of `configure` (`django/conf/__init__.py:_check_email_settings_conflicts`); `override_settings` does not check, and an email setting it sets beside `MAILERS` is refused when read.

Since 5.2 the `TEMPLATES` of the settings module that startproject writes omits the debug context processor, which still exists (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`, `django/template/context_processors.py:debug`).

Since 5.2 the `TEMPLATES` of the settings module that startproject writes omits the debug context processor, which still exists (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`, `django/template/context_processors.py:debug`).

Since 6.0 that module sets no `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD`, and the `AppConfig` that startapp writes no `AppConfig.default_auto_field` (`django/conf/app_template/apps.py-tpl`): both named `BigAutoField`, which 6.0 made the setting's default ([What changed in models and fields](models.md)).

Since 6.2 `ManagementUtility.fetch_command` then refuses, with that message and status 1, a command whose `BaseCommand.requires_settings` is true, the default (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.fetch_command`).
Before, the notes say, an `ImportError` from the settings module was suppressed for every command (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

Since 5.2 `BaseCommand.execute` asks `BaseCommand.get_check_kwargs` for the arguments of its call of `BaseCommand.check`, a method a command may override (`django/core/management/base.py:BaseCommand.get_check_kwargs`). migrate overrides it to add its database, whose checks then run before it migrates; runserver returns an empty collection of tags, which selects nothing, and runs them itself in the serving process ([The development server](../commands/runserver.md)).

Since 6.1 `CheckRegistry.run_checks` gives the check functions every configured alias when its caller leaves the databases argument at None, where it used to give none (`django/core/checks/registry.py:CheckRegistry.run_checks`).

The change reaches the checks that work per database, among them the model checks of long column names, indexes, constraints and table comments (`django/db/models/base.py:Model.check`) and the fields' checks that ask the backend (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._check_backend_specific_checks`): they now run against the connection of each alias the router lets the model migrate to, and where a backend learns its features from the server, as MySQL's does, the first read of one connects (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.mysql_server_data`).

Callers, the notes say, "should be prepared for databases to be accessed" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`; [The system checks](../commands/checks.md)).

`Command.get_auto_imports` returns dotted paths to import, among them every model that `Apps.get_models` returns, which leaves out the automatic through models of many-to-many relations and swapped models (`django/core/management/commands/shell.py:Command.get_auto_imports`).
